title: RAFAELIA Stack v5.0.0 — Deterministic low-level compiler from speech to bytecode with multilingual biblical corpus and toroidal cognitive kernel
description:
RAFAELIA is a 295KB / 6,432-line source stack delivering an end-to-end pipeline from human speech → tokens → AST → bytecode → ARM64/x86_64 assembly → execution, validated on real hardware (Motorola E7 Power, Cortex-A55, Android 10, Termux).

The stack closes the gap between heavyweight ML frameworks (libtorch, ONNX Runtime, 5–50 MB binaries) and minimal embedded libraries that lack cognition, providing:

  • FALA → LOW-LEVEL compiler across 7 languages (Portuguese, Hebrew, Aramaic, Greek, Latin, Japanese, Chinese) with 60 reusable AI seeds (T01–T12 × A–E)
  • C runtime dual-mode (libc + freestanding, 32 opcodes, direct syscall) producing a 16KB binary
  • Cognitive kernel implementing the ψ→χ→ρ→Δ→Σ→Ω cycle with 5 operational modes (cognitive, physical, cryptographic, distributed, autopoietic)
  • Biblical corpus of 12 canonical verses pre-compiled with gematria (Hebrew + Greek, NFD-normalized), bytecode, and ARM64 assembly
  • Mathematical framework with 110+ original formulas (toroidal T⁷, Fibonacci-Rafael recursion, Φ_ethica filter)
  • 90 Termux sensor seeds (S00–S17 × A–E) covering microphone-entropy, IMU-toroidal-mapping, magnetic-SLAM, BLE-mesh, NFC-mesh, IR-covert-channel, and more

Validation: 230+ unit tests passing, 18/18 smoke tests green, build-reproducible tarball (deterministic mtime, owner, sort order), SHA256 + Merkle root verifiable end-to-end.

Reproducibility: 60 seconds from tarball to running demo on any POSIX bash + clang + python3.
